_meta.title: helvetic APM machine-readable ruleset
_meta.scope: APM Chapter 1 (language, all publications) and Chapter 3.2 (WebManuals styling)
_meta.source_document: APM - Administrative Procedure Manual, Issue 01 Rev 19 (06.01.2026)
_meta.generated_for: generate-check pipeline: generator consumes 'prompt_fragment', verifier consumes 'check'

_schema.description: Each object in 'rules' has the fields below.

fields.id: stable identifier, matches the markdown ruleset
fields.source: APM section(s) the rule derives from
fields.category: terminology | capitalisation | grammar | tone | units | references | bullets | line_breaks | headings | tables | notes | colours | cross_references | emphasis | process
fields.conditional: true if correctness depends on surrounding context/state, not a line-by-line match
fields.prompt_fragment: terse instruction injected into the generator system prompt; present for every rule
fields.check: verifier spec; present only where automatable. 'kind' dispatches the check.

check_kinds.style_constant: property, value (a value the generator/styler must emit; verify against html)
check_kinds.consolidated: ref (id) — literal check lives under another rule to avoid double-flagging

rules.statement: Target reader is a non-native English speaker with average English but good aviation knowledge; match complexity accordingly.
rules.prompt_fragment: Write for a non-native English speaker with average English and good aviation knowledge; keep complexity appropriate to that reader.

rules.statement: Fact-/evidence-based, professional, respectful; clear, concise, exact and distinct.
rules.prompt_fragment: Be fact-based, professional and respectful; write clear, concise, exact and distinct sentences.

rules.statement: No nested/convoluted sentences (no Schachtelsaetze).
rules.prompt_fragment: Avoid long nested sentences; prefer short, direct constructions.

rules.statement: Do not use directly translated Swiss German.
rules.prompt_fragment: Do not use directly translated Swiss German phrasing or word order.

rules.statement: 'helvetic' (brand) is always lowercase, even at the start of a sentence/title; never italic.
rules.prompt_fragment: Always write the brand as lowercase 'helvetic', even at the start of a sentence or title, and never in italics. Capitalise only inside the legal name 'Helvetic Airways AG'.

check.notes: Helvetic/helvetic literal check lives in the term table; italic check requires html target.

rules.statement: Capitalise 'Helvetic' only within the full legal name 'Helvetic Airways AG' (or 'Helvetic Airways').
rules.prompt_fragment: Use the capitalised 'Helvetic' only as part of 'Helvetic Airways AG' or 'Helvetic Airways'.

rules.statement: Forbidden mixed company-name forms: 'helvetic Airways', 'Helvetic airways', 'helvetic airways'.
rules.prompt_fragment: Never use mixed forms such as 'helvetic Airways', 'Helvetic airways' or 'helvetic airways'.

rules.statement: Use 'helvetic Part-145' (lowercase helvetic, capital P, hyphen). May shorten to 'Part-145' after first mention in a chapter.
rules.prompt_fragment: Write 'helvetic Part-145' on first mention in a chapter; thereafter 'Part-145' alone is acceptable. Never 'Part M', 'Part-M' or 'part 145'.

rules.statement: Forbidden: 'Part M', 'Part-M'.
rules.prompt_fragment: Do not use 'Part M' or 'Part-M'.

rules.statement: Countries, places and languages are capitalised (Switzerland, Zurich, Swedish, British).
rules.prompt_fragment: Capitalise names of countries, places and languages.

rules.statement: Titles: first word capitalised and all nouns/subjects capitalised (e.g. 'Recent Experience for Flight Crew').
rules.prompt_fragment: In titles, capitalise the first word and every noun and subject (e.g. 'Recent Experience for Flight Crew').

rules.statement: General function descriptions are lowercase ('flight crews', 'nominated persons').
rules.prompt_fragment: Write general function descriptions in lowercase ('flight crews', 'nominated persons').

rules.statement: Specific job titles are capitalised and followed by the abbreviation in brackets on first use (e.g. 'Safety Manager (SM)').
rules.prompt_fragment: Capitalise specific job titles and give the abbreviation in brackets on first use (e.g. 'Head of Inflight Product (HIP)').

rules.statement: All abbreviations are written in capitals (FOP, ACM, HIP).
rules.prompt_fragment: Write all abbreviations in capitals.

rules.statement: On first use, give the full designation followed by the abbreviation in brackets ('Emergency Response Plan (ERP)').
rules.prompt_fragment: Introduce each abbreviation on first use as 'Full Designation (ABBR)', then use the abbreviation alone thereafter.

rules.statement: When used alone (after introduction), abbreviations are capitals with no brackets.
rules.prompt_fragment: After introduction, use the abbreviation in capitals without brackets.

rules.statement: Stand-alone abbreviations (never expanded) only if undoubtedly well-known (ATC, ZRH, LX) and/or set as an active tooltip abbreviation.
rules.prompt_fragment: Use a stand-alone, unexplained abbreviation only when it is universally known in aviation (e.g. ATC, ZRH, LX).

rules.statement: No imperatives/command tone (Befehlston); use passive voice. e.g. 'cleaning staff shall be instructed to', not 'instruct cleaning staff to'.
rules.prompt_fragment: Use passive, fact-based voice rather than imperatives: 'X shall be done', not 'do X'.

rules.statement: 'etc.' is forbidden; complete the text and add examples in brackets instead.
rules.prompt_fragment: Never use 'etc.'. List the items, adding examples in brackets where helpful.

rules.statement: Count-up/listing logic: in a bullet count-up items are linked by 'and' unless 'or' is explicitly stated between the lines; in a listing 'or' is non-exclusive (one, several, or all may apply).
rules.prompt_fragment: Treat bullet count-ups as 'and' unless 'or' is explicitly written; treat 'or' in any listing as non-exclusive.

rules.statement: Modal verbs: 'shall'/'must' (or imperative action verb) = mandatory ('must' is an alternative to 'shall'); 'should' = recommended AND must state the circumstances under which it need not be applied; 'may' = optional.
rules.prompt_fragment: Use 'shall'/'must' for mandatory, 'should' for recommended, 'may' for optional. Whenever you write 'should', also state the circumstances under which the provision need not be applied.

check.requires: a nearby clause stating when the provision does not have to be applied

rules.statement: 'approved (by the authority)' = documented by the authority as suitable for the purpose intended; 'accepted/acceptable' = not objected to by the authority as suitable for the purpose intended.
rules.prompt_fragment: Use 'approved' = documented by the authority as suitable; 'accepted/acceptable' = not objected to by the authority. Do not interchange them.

rules.statement: 'bi-weekly' means every two weeks; the 'bi-' convention applies to any time interval.
rules.prompt_fragment: Use 'bi-weekly' to mean every two weeks (the 'bi-' convention applies to any interval).

rules.statement: No contractions; use full forms ('do not', 'will not', 'it is').
rules.prompt_fragment: Never use contractions; always write full forms ('do not', 'will not', 'it is').

check.notes: Excludes genitives like UFO's which are valid; review flags.

rules.statement: 'aircraft' and 'information' have no separate plural form ('two aircraft').
rules.prompt_fragment: Never write 'aircrafts' or 'informations'; the plural equals the singular.

rules.statement: Plural takes no apostrophe; apostrophe only for genitive (wrong: 'AMC's', 'CS's').
rules.prompt_fragment: Do not use an apostrophe to form plurals of abbreviations ('AMCs', not 'AMC's').

check.notes: Genitive use is valid; review flags.

rules.statement: Observe 'it's' (it is) vs 'its' (possessive). (Combined with no-contractions, 'it's' should not appear at all.)
rules.prompt_fragment: Use 'its' for possessive; never 'it's' (also barred by the no-contractions rule).

rules.statement: 'participate' is followed by 'in'.
rules.prompt_fragment: Follow 'participate' with 'in' ('participated in a meeting').

rules.statement: 'following' introducing a list is preceded by 'the' ('the following regulations apply:'). Exception: temporal use ('Following a meeting, ...').
rules.prompt_fragment: When 'following' introduces a list, precede it with 'the' ('the following ... apply:'); not for temporal use.

rules.statement: Use 'i.e.' (restates/clarifies) vs 'e.g.' (gives examples) correctly.
rules.prompt_fragment: Use 'i.e.' to restate/clarify and 'e.g.' to give examples; do not swap them.

rules.statement: Non-English words are written in italics (e.g. Zivilgesetzbuch (ZGB)).
rules.prompt_fragment: Italicise any non-English words.

rules.statement: Uniform spelling of specific terms: use the correct form, flag the forbidden form(s).
rules.prompt_fragment: Use these exact forms: according to; callout; checklist; email; Flightops; helvetic (brand); Helvetic Airways AG; nominated person; Operations Manuals; Operations Management; Operations Control Center; helvetic Part-145; Piquet Officer (PQO); registration; SharePoint; straightforward.

terms.notes: Brand alone; 'Helvetic' valid only in 'Helvetic Airways AG'.

rules.statement: Space between numerical value and SI unit ('250 g', '250 kts', '10000 ft', '3 h', '15 s').
rules.prompt_fragment: Put a space between a number and its SI unit ('250 kts', '10000 ft').

check.rule: require space between number and SI unit symbol

rules.statement: No space for: percentages (30%), typographic units (12pt, 10px), angles/degrees (30deg, 45deg, 22').
rules.prompt_fragment: No space before %, pt, px, or degree/angle symbols.

rules.statement: Temperature: '30 C' (with space) technically correct, '30C' tolerated.
rules.prompt_fragment: For temperatures, a space before the degree-C is preferred but the no-space form is tolerated.

rules.statement: Currency: symbol no space ($10); unit with space (10 USD).
rules.prompt_fragment: Currency symbol takes no space ('$10'); currency unit takes a space ('10 USD').

rules.statement: Time of day: no space ('3PM', '6PM').
rules.prompt_fragment: Write time of day with no space ('3PM').

rules.statement: Spaces may be dropped for conciseness (checklists/procedures) or for chapter consistency.
rules.prompt_fragment: In checklists/procedures, the number-unit space may be dropped for conciseness or to keep a chapter consistent.

rules.statement: Crew terms: 'cabin crew' (whole) / 'cabin crew member' (single) / 'flight crew' (whole, flight deck) / 'flight crew member' (single).
rules.prompt_fragment: Use 'cabin crew'/'flight crew' for the whole crew and 'cabin crew member'/'flight crew member' for an individual.

rules.statement: Refer to software/hardware tools by purpose, not brand. Brand allowed only in technical/tool-specific sections, and only if known or introduced. Tool-name list in OM-0 11.
rules.prompt_fragment: Refer to software/hardware tools by their purpose, not their brand name, unless the section is specifically technical about that tool.

rules.statement: Qualification requirements use the sequence Facts -> Training and Experience -> Skills -> Knowledge (may combine if few). Language is listed under Skills, first in the Skills list.
rules.prompt_fragment: Order qualification requirements as Facts, Training and Experience, Skills, Knowledge; list language under Skills (first).

rules.statement: Prefer a reference over copying source content.
rules.prompt_fragment: Reference the source section instead of copying its content.

rules.statement: A reference must include the section title, not just the number ('refer to OM-D 2.7.1.3 Training Effectiveness').
rules.prompt_fragment: Every reference must include the section title as well as its number.

rules.statement: No chains of references; point directly to the source text.
rules.prompt_fragment: Point references directly at the source text, never at another reference.

rules.statement: The addressed reader must legally have access to any referenced document.
rules.prompt_fragment: Only reference documents the intended reader is entitled to access by their role.

rules.statement: Intro sentence + each bullet must read as one grammatically correct sentence.
rules.prompt_fragment: Make the lead-in line and every bullet combine into a grammatically correct sentence.

rules.statement: One empty line between main bullets; may be omitted to fit a page.
rules.prompt_fragment: Separate main bullets with one empty line.

check.description: main-level list items separated by spacing

rules.statement: No empty line between sub-bullets (unless they contain long text).
rules.prompt_fragment: Do not add empty lines between sub-bullets unless they hold long text.

rules.statement: No extra space before a list; at least two breaks after a list.
rules.prompt_fragment: Add no extra space before a bullet list; follow it with at least two line breaks.

rules.statement: Each bullet starts lowercase, except terms normally capitalised ('Safety Manager (SM)', 'Finland').
rules.prompt_fragment: Start each bullet with a lowercase letter unless it begins with a normally-capitalised term.

rules.statement: No full stop on short/partial-sentence bullets; full stop only when a bullet holds longer text with multiple sentences.
rules.prompt_fragment: Do not end short bullets with a full stop; use one only for bullets containing multiple sentences.

rules.statement: Soft break (Shift+Enter) for styling within a continuous paragraph.
rules.prompt_fragment: Use a soft break for line styling inside one continuous paragraph.

rules.statement: One hard break to separate paragraphs on a similar topic.
rules.prompt_fragment: Separate same-topic paragraphs with one hard break.

rules.statement: Two hard breaks to separate paragraphs on different topics (when no subheading is used).
rules.prompt_fragment: Separate different-topic paragraphs with two hard breaks when no subheading is used.

rules.statement: Use auto-numbered headings (Heading 2-8); numbering mandatory. Heading 1 reserved for chapter dividers; Heading 2 is the highest manual level.
rules.prompt_fragment: Use numbered Heading 2-8 for subtitles; do not assign Heading 1 (reserved for chapter dividers).

check.description: headings use h2-h8; no manual h1

rules.statement: Heading-2 subchapters normally start on a new page; if short ones share a page, add a line break before each.
rules.prompt_fragment: Start Heading-2 subchapters on a new page; if grouping short ones, add a line break before each.

rules.statement: Heading 3-8 need no extra break before them (may add for readability).
rules.prompt_fragment: No extra break is needed before Heading 3-8.

rules.statement: Unnumbered subtitles: main subtitle bold, subordinate subtitle italic (sparingly). Two hard breaks before, one hard break after.
rules.prompt_fragment: For unnumbered subtitles use bold (main) / italic (subordinate); two hard breaks before, one after.

rules.statement: Table width 500px standard; 100% (=720px) for more content; rotate 90deg for very wide tables.
rules.prompt_fragment: Use 500px table width by default, 100% for content-heavy tables.

rules.statement: Simple/frequently changed -> build natively; complex/rarely changed -> embed as image.
rules.prompt_fragment: Build simple, frequently changed tables natively; embed complex, rarely changed tables as images.

rules.statement: Vertical alignment top for multi-line cells; horizontal left by default.
rules.prompt_fragment: Align multi-line cell content to top; left-align horizontally by default.

rules.statement: First row marked as header (first column in exceptional cases).
rules.prompt_fragment: Mark the first row as the table header.

rules.statement: Optional emphasis colours: main title row #bbbbbb bold; subtitle row #dddddd normal; content #ffffff normal.
rules.prompt_fragment: If colouring table rows: main title #bbbbbb bold, subtitle #dddddd normal, content #ffffff.

rules.statement: Keep tables of similar layout on the same page.
rules.prompt_fragment: Group tables of similar layout on the same page.

rules.statement: Colours: Note emerald #2ecc71; Caution orange #f39c12; Warning pale red #e74c3c.
rules.prompt_fragment: Colour Notes #2ecc71, Cautions #f39c12, Warnings #e74c3c.

rules.statement: Unnumbered note: table 100%, first column 60px, border 0px.
rules.prompt_fragment: Unnumbered note layout: table 100%, first column 60px, border 0.

rules.statement: Numbered note: table 100%, first column 110px, border 0px; in-text reference green, superscript, 14pt, in brackets.
rules.prompt_fragment: Numbered note layout: table 100%, first column 110px, border 0; reference green superscript 14pt in brackets.

rules.statement: Caution/Warning: table 100%, first column 110px, border 0px.
rules.prompt_fragment: Caution/Warning layout: table 100%, first column 110px, border 0.

rules.statement: First sentence of any Note/Caution/Warning starts with a capital letter.
rules.prompt_fragment: Start the first sentence of every Note/Caution/Warning with a capital letter.

rules.statement: Urgency messages: Warning #e74c3c, Caution #f39c12, Advisory #3498db, Note #2ecc71.
rules.prompt_fragment: Urgency colours: Warning #e74c3c, Caution #f39c12, Advisory #3498db, Note #2ecc71.

rules.statement: Embraer fleet variant colours (use uniformly): E1 #019A82, E190-E1 #02cda5 (bg #dcf2ee), E195-E1 #00665e (bg #94b3b0), E2 #002CAD, E190-E2 #0057d9 (bg #ccdce8), E195-E2 #000080 (bg #bec6d1).
rules.prompt_fragment: Use the assigned Embraer variant colours uniformly (E190-E1 #02cda5, E195-E1 #00665e, E190-E2 #0057d9, E195-E2 #000080, etc.).

rules.statement: Good/bad table cell shading (use conservatively): good #f5fcf5, bad #f7e9e9.
rules.prompt_fragment: For good/bad table cells use good=#f5fcf5, bad=#f7e9e9, sparingly.

rules.statement: Grey titles: #848687, 24px.
rules.prompt_fragment: Grey titles use #848687 at 24px.

rules.statement: References as active (clickable) links, internal and external.
rules.prompt_fragment: Render references as active links, internal and external.

rules.statement: Mark links as 'Controlled Link' for tracking.
rules.prompt_fragment: Set every reference link as a 'Controlled Link'.

rules.statement: Link to headings, not pages.
rules.prompt_fragment: Link to headings rather than pages.

rules.statement: Internal reference: section only ('3.2.6.3 - Marking / Colouring').
rules.prompt_fragment: Write internal references as section only (e.g. '3.2.6.3 - Title').

rules.statement: External reference: prefix with the manual name ('OM-A 8.3.8.5 Wind Shear').
rules.prompt_fragment: Prefix external references with the manual name (e.g. 'OM-A 8.3.8.5 Wind Shear').

rules.statement: Bold/underline very conservatively, a few words at most, only for crucial items or to prevent error.
rules.prompt_fragment: Use bold/underline only for a few crucial words, never for whole sentences.

rules.statement: No manual font/size changes; use the standard WebManuals font/size.
rules.prompt_fragment: Do not change font or size; use the standard body style.

rules.statement: Clear imported formatting (Remove Format) when pasting from external sources.
rules.prompt_fragment: Strip imported formatting so output carries no foreign fonts/colours/sizes.

rules.statement: Changelog comments: 2-3 per change (content; reference/reason; MoC for prior approval). 'Important' flag only for prior-approval or reader-attention content comments.
rules.prompt_fragment: (Process) Each change needs a content comment, a reference/reason comment, and an MoC comment if prior approval applies.

rules.statement: Content mirroring: mirror from the NEXT revision of the source; use the offset function for heading levels.
rules.prompt_fragment: (Process) Mirror content from the next revision of the source, adjusting heading levels via offset.

rules.statement: Abbreviations are auto-detected, created/used via pop-up, marked yellow, and auto-listed in the LoA.
rules.prompt_fragment: (Process) Confirm abbreviations via the WebManuals pop-up so they appear in the List of Abbreviations.
